transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi. I came in because I've been having some trouble with my eating habits. It usually happens after everyone goes to bed. I’ll tell myself I’m just going to have some leftovers, and then... I realize I’ve eaten half a tray of catered pasta from work, the dessert from a client dinner, and whatever snacks were in the pantry, all in one sitting.
After an episode like that, do you do anything to try to prevent weight gain, such as making yourself vomit, taking laxatives, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do any of that. I don't make myself throw up, and I've never taken laxatives or anything. And I definitely don't exercise excessively. I mostly just... I just kind of sit there feeling awful about it afterwards, but I don't try to undo it like that.
During these times when you are eating, do you feel like you can't stop or can't control how much you're eating?

Yes, that's exactly it. Once I start—especially if it's been a tense night with my husband—it feels like the decision-making part of my brain just goes completely offline. I'll keep reaching for more food, even while I'm actively thinking to myself, 'Patricia, stop, this is enough.' But I just can't seem to make myself stop.
On average, how many times a week do these episodes happen?

For the last three months or so, there's been at least one night almost every week where I end up eating like this. It usually happens after an argument, or maybe a late work event. And... well, some weeks it happens twice.
